items.meaning: To ensure you do something because it's important or you want to.
items.example: I always make a point of learning a few local phrases when I travel.
items.plain: I always try to learn some local phrases when I travel.
items.note: Emphasizes intentionality; shows a deliberate action.

items.meaning: To finally do something after a delay or procrastination.
items.example: I need to get around to booking my train tickets for next week.
items.plain: I need to book my train tickets for next week soon.
items.note: Implies a task that has been pending for a while.

items.meaning: At the appropriate time in the future, eventually.
items.example: Your luggage will be delivered to your hotel in due course.
items.plain: Your luggage will be delivered to your hotel when it's ready.
items.note: Formal and reassuring, often used by service staff.

items.meaning: To remember or consider something important.
items.example: Bear in mind that the museum closes early on Sundays.
items.plain: Remember that the museum closes early on Sundays.
items.note: A polite way to give a reminder or important information.

items.meaning: For now; temporarily.
items.example: We'll stay at this hotel for the time being until our apartment is ready.
items.plain: We'll stay at this hotel temporarily.
items.note: Indicates a temporary arrangement or situation.

items.meaning: Used to confirm or correct information, often with a slight surprise.
items.example: "Are you heading to the airport?" "As a matter of fact, I am."
items.plain: "Are you heading to the airport?" "Yes, I am."
items.note: Adds emphasis or a touch of mild irony; can sound slightly formal.

items.meaning: Definitely not; not at all.
items.example: The journey was by no means easy, but the destination was worth it.
items.plain: The journey was not easy at all, but the destination was worth it.
items.note: Strong emphasis on negation; sounds quite formal.

items.meaning: After reconsidering something; changing one's mind.
items.example: I'll take the bus, but on second thought, maybe a taxi would be faster.
items.plain: I'll take the bus, but I've changed my mind, a taxi might be faster.
items.note: Common in casual speech when revising a decision.

items.meaning: Partially; not entirely.
items.example: The new travel restrictions will affect our plans to some extent.
items.plain: The new travel restrictions will partially affect our plans.
items.note: A common hedge, softening a statement or making it less absolute.

items.meaning: Over a long period of time; eventually.
items.example: Booking flights in advance might seem restrictive, but it saves money in the long run.
items.plain: Booking flights in advance saves money eventually.
items.note: Refers to future consequences or benefits.

items.meaning: As soon as you can; as soon as it is easy for you.
items.example: Please contact the front desk at your earliest convenience to confirm your departure.
items.plain: Please contact the front desk as soon as you can to confirm your departure.
items.note: Very formal and polite, typically used in written or official requests.

items.meaning: To learn how to do something, especially something new or tricky.
items.example: It took me a while to get the hang of using the local public transport system.
items.plain: It took me a while to learn how to use the local public transport system.
items.note: Informal and common, implies a learning curve.

items.meaning: To state something clearly and officially, often to ensure it's noted.
items.example: For the record, I did try to call the airline multiple times about the delay.
items.plain: I want to state that I called the airline many times about the delay.
items.note: Used to emphasize a statement's importance or accuracy.

items.meaning: Generally speaking; considering everything.
items.example: On the whole, our trip was fantastic despite a few minor hiccups.
items.plain: Generally, our trip was fantastic despite a few minor problems.
items.note: Used to summarize an overall impression or opinion.

items.meaning: Mostly; generally.
items.example: By and large, the local cuisine here is delicious and very affordable.
items.plain: Mostly, the local food here is delicious and very affordable.
items.note: Similar to "on the whole," often used for general observations.

items.meaning: In my opinion; from my perspective.
items.example: As far as I'm concerned, the best way to see the city is on foot.
items.plain: In my opinion, the best way to see the city is on foot.
items.note: Expresses a personal opinion, can sometimes sound a little assertive.

items.meaning: To summarize something very briefly.
items.example: In a nutshell, our flight was delayed, we missed our connection, and our luggage is lost.
items.plain: To summarize, our flight was delayed, we missed our connection, and our luggage is lost.
items.note: Informal and concise, used for quick summaries.

items.meaning: According to your own judgment or choice.
items.example: You can choose your departure time at your discretion, within the operating hours.
items.plain: You can choose your departure time yourself.
items.note: Formal, grants freedom of choice to the other person.

items.meaning: Without any more delay or fuss.
items.example: Without further ado, let's head to the airport to catch our flight.
items.plain: Let's go to the airport now to catch our flight.
items.note: Slightly formal, often used to transition to an action.

items.text: to cut a long story short
items.form: to cut a long story short
items.meaning: To tell the main points of a story quickly.
items.example: To cut a long story short, we eventually found our way back to the hotel.
items.plain: We eventually found our way back to the hotel.
items.note: Informal, used when you want to get to the point quickly.

items.meaning: To consider something when making a decision or judgment.
items.example: We need to take into account the local customs when planning our itinerary.
items.plain: We need to consider the local customs when planning our itinerary.
items.note: Important for planning and showing cultural sensitivity.

items.meaning: To come to an agreement where both sides give up something.
items.example: We had to reach a compromise on our travel dates due to conflicting schedules.
items.plain: We had to agree on travel dates by both giving in a little.
items.note: Used when negotiating or resolving differences.

items.meaning: To resolve small problems or finalize specific arrangements.
items.example: We still need to iron out the details for our airport transfer.
items.plain: We still need to finalize the arrangements for our airport transfer.
items.note: Informal and common, implies resolving minor issues.

items.meaning: To take advantage of a chance quickly and eagerly.
items.example: We decided to seize the opportunity to visit the ancient ruins while we were nearby.
items.plain: We decided to take the chance to visit the ancient ruins while we were nearby.
items.note: Suggests enthusiasm and quick action.

items.meaning: To form an opinion or judgment after considering information.
items.example: It's too early to draw a conclusion about the overall success of the trip.
items.plain: It's too early to decide if the trip was successful.
items.note: Formal, used in analytical or evaluative contexts.

items.meaning: To find a satisfactory compromise between two opposing things.
items.example: We tried to strike a balance between sightseeing and relaxation on our vacation.
items.plain: We tried to find a good mix of sightseeing and relaxation on our vacation.
items.note: Common for describing efforts to achieve equilibrium.

items.meaning: To create pressure or tension, potentially causing difficulties.
items.example: The unexpected flight delay really put a strain on our travel budget.
items.plain: The unexpected flight delay really stressed our travel budget.
items.note: Used to describe something that causes stress or difficulty.

items.meaning: To accept and deal with a difficult situation or fact.
items.example: It took me a while to come to terms with the fact that my luggage was truly lost.
items.plain: It took me a while to accept that my luggage was truly lost.
items.note: Implies a process of acceptance, often for something negative.

items.meaning: To focus on or notice something carefully.
items.example: You should pay attention to the safety briefing before the flight.
items.plain: You should listen carefully to the safety briefing before the flight.
items.note: A common instruction or recommendation.

items.meaning: To be the first to act or make a decision, without being told.
items.example: When our tour guide was late, I decided to take the initiative and find out what was happening.
items.plain: When our tour guide was late, I decided to act first and find out what was happening.
items.note: Praises proactive behavior; often used in professional contexts.

items.meaning: To do the same thing as someone else has just done.
items.example: When one passenger complained about the food, others quickly followed suit.
items.plain: When one passenger complained about the food, others did the same.
items.note: Common in describing group behavior or trends.

items.meaning: To watch something or someone carefully.
items.example: Could you keep an eye on my bags while I go to the restroom?
items.plain: Could you watch my bags while I go to the restroom?
items.note: Informal and very common, used for temporary supervision.

items.meaning: To no longer know where something is or what is happening.
items.example: I often lose track of time when I'm exploring a new city.
items.plain: I often forget what time it is when I'm exploring a new city.
items.note: Common for describing a lapse in awareness.

items.meaning: To postpone or delay doing something.
items.example: We had to put off our trip until next month due to unforeseen circumstances.
items.plain: We had to delay our trip until next month.
items.note: Very common phrasal verb, informal.

items.meaning: To form an idea or opinion about something, often based on indirect evidence.
items.example: I get the impression that the hotel staff are a bit overwhelmed today.
items.plain: I think the hotel staff are a bit overwhelmed today.
items.note: A polite way to express an observation or feeling without stating it as fact.

items.meaning: To take a longer, indirect route to a destination.
items.example: We had to take a detour because the main road was closed for repairs.
items.plain: We had to go a different, longer way because the main road was closed.
items.note: Common in travel contexts, literal or figurative.

items.meaning: To encounter difficulties or problems.
items.example: We might run into trouble if we don't have our visas sorted out before we leave.
items.plain: We might have problems if we don't have our visas sorted out.
items.note: Informal and common, implies unexpected difficulties.

items.meaning: To stay informed about the latest news or developments.
items.example: It's important to keep abreast of the local travel advisories.
items.plain: It's important to stay informed about the local travel advisories.
items.note: Slightly formal, suggests staying current with information.

items.meaning: To plan and prepare for something.
items.example: We need to make arrangements for our accommodation in advance.
items.plain: We need to plan our accommodation in advance.
items.note: Common for planning events or travel.

items.meaning: To relieve someone's worry or anxiety.
items.example: The hotel manager's quick response really put my mind at ease about the lost key.
items.plain: The hotel manager's quick response made me stop worrying about the lost key.
items.note: Used when someone's concerns are alleviated.

items.meaning: To clarify the main point or intention of what you are saying.
items.example: What I'm getting at is, we should probably leave earlier to avoid traffic.
items.plain: My main point is that we should probably leave earlier to avoid traffic.
items.note: Used to explain or summarize your underlying message.

items.meaning: To introduce an important point, explanation, or problem.
items.example: The thing is, I don't have any local currency on me right now.
items.plain: The problem is, I don't have any local currency on me right now.
items.note: Very common and informal, often used to explain a difficulty.

items.meaning: To reveal information that was previously unknown or unexpected.
items.example: It turns out that our flight was actually delayed by three hours, not one.
items.plain: We discovered that our flight was actually delayed by three hours.
items.note: Used to introduce a discovery or unexpected fact.

items.meaning: A very polite and indirect way to ask a question or make a request.
items.example: I was wondering if you could recommend a good local restaurant.
items.plain: Could you recommend a good local restaurant?
items.note: Extremely polite, suitable for asking strangers or service staff.

items.meaning: A polite way to interrupt or interject, often to ask a question or make a point.
items.example: If I could just ask, what time does the last bus leave for the city center?
items.plain: What time does the last bus leave for the city center?
items.note: Used to politely gain attention or interject.

items.meaning: To state the reason for a phone call directly.
items.example: I'm calling about a reservation I made for next week.
items.plain: I'm calling because of a reservation I made for next week.
items.note: Standard and clear way to open a phone conversation.

items.meaning: To clarify or rephrase something you've just said.
items.example: The hotel is a bit far, what I mean is, it's not within walking distance of the attractions.
items.plain: The hotel is a bit far; it's not within walking distance of the attractions.
items.note: Used to elaborate or make a statement clearer.

items.meaning: To emphasize the most important aspect of what you are saying.
items.example: The point is, we need to find a solution to this luggage issue quickly.
items.plain: The most important thing is that we need to solve this luggage issue quickly.
items.note: Direct and assertive, used to highlight importance.

items.meaning: A polite way to introduce bad news or a negative statement.
items.example: I'm afraid that your flight has been cancelled due to bad weather.
items.plain: Your flight has been cancelled due to bad weather.
items.note: Softens negative information, showing regret.

items.meaning: To express an opinion or observation, often cautiously.
items.example: It seems to me that the train schedule has changed recently.
items.plain: I think the train schedule has changed recently.
items.note: A polite and indirect way to offer an opinion.

items.meaning: A formal and polite way to ask for information.
items.example: I'd like to inquire about the availability of a room for tonight.
items.plain: I want to ask about the availability of a room for tonight.
items.note: Formal and professional, suitable for customer service interactions.

items.meaning: A polite and common way to ask for information.
items.example: Could you tell me how to get to the nearest bus stop from here?
items.plain: How do I get to the nearest bus stop from here?
items.note: Standard polite question, widely applicable.

items.text: I'm having a bit of trouble with
items.form: I'm having a bit of trouble with
items.meaning: A polite and understated way to explain a problem you are experiencing.
items.example: I'm having a bit of trouble with the Wi-Fi connection in my room.
items.plain: The Wi-Fi connection in my room isn't working well.
items.note: Softens a complaint, making it less direct.

items.meaning: To introduce the main difficulty or obstacle.
items.example: The problem is that we don't have enough time to visit all the museums.
items.plain: We don't have enough time to visit all the museums.
items.note: Direct and clear, used to state a specific issue.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to verify details.
items.example: I'm calling to confirm my flight details for tomorrow morning.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify my flight details for tomorrow morning.
items.note: Standard and efficient for phone calls.

items.meaning: To introduce an important piece of information that should be remembered.
items.example: It's worth noting that the local market is only open on weekends.
items.plain: Remember that the local market is only open on weekends.
items.note: Highlights important information, often a useful tip.

items.meaning: To state what you are trying to find.
items.example: I'm looking for a good coffee shop with Wi-Fi nearby.
items.plain: I want to find a good coffee shop with Wi-Fi nearby.
items.note: Simple and direct, common for asking directions or recommendations.

items.text: What I'd like to do is
items.form: What I'd like to do is
items.meaning: To state your intention or preference.
items.example: What I'd like to do is reschedule my train ticket for later today.
items.plain: I want to reschedule my train ticket for later today.
items.note: A polite and slightly indirect way to express a desire.

items.meaning: To explain your current goal or effort.
items.example: I'm trying to find the departure gate for flight BA249.
items.plain: I want to find the departure gate for flight BA249.
items.note: Common when asking for help with a task.

items.meaning: A very polite and tentative way to make a request.
items.example: Could you possibly help me with my luggage up the stairs?
items.plain: Could you help me with my luggage up the stairs?
items.note: Extremely polite, used for requests that might be inconvenient.

items.meaning: A formal way to state the purpose of a call, seeking information.
items.example: I'm calling to inquire about the status of my lost baggage claim.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask about my lost baggage claim.
items.note: Formal and professional, suitable for customer service.

items.meaning: To emphasize a crucial piece of information.
items.example: It's important to remember that some shops close for a siesta in the afternoon.
items.plain: Remember that some shops close for a siesta in the afternoon.
items.note: Highlights a key point, often a warning or useful tip.

items.meaning: A casual and polite way to verify information.
items.example: I'm just checking if my room reservation includes breakfast.
items.plain: Does my room reservation include breakfast?
items.note: Informal and common, used for quick verification.

items.meaning: A very polite and formal way to make a request.
items.example: I'd be grateful if you could provide a map of the local area.
items.plain: Please provide a map of the local area.
items.note: Formal and deferential, often used in written communication or formal requests.

items.meaning: A polite way to decline or state a lack of knowledge.
items.example: I'm afraid I don't speak the local language very well.
items.plain: I don't speak the local language very well.
items.note: Softens a negative statement, showing regret.

items.meaning: To offer advice or a recommendation.
items.example: It's a good idea to carry a copy of your passport when exploring.
items.plain: You should carry a copy of your passport when exploring.
items.note: Common for giving practical advice.

items.meaning: A formal way to state the subject of a phone call.
items.example: I'm calling regarding the delayed flight to London.
items.plain: I'm calling about the delayed flight to London.
items.note: Formal and professional, used in business or customer service.

items.meaning: A polite and formal way to state a problem you are experiencing.
items.example: I'm having difficulty with the online check-in process.
items.plain: I'm finding the online check-in process difficult.
items.note: More formal than "a bit of trouble," suitable for official complaints.

items.meaning: To express a desire or plan, often with a hint of uncertainty.
items.example: I'm hoping to catch the early train to avoid the rush hour.
items.plain: I want to catch the early train to avoid the rush hour.
items.note: Softer than "I want to," implies a wish or plan.

items.meaning: A casual and polite way to ask a question or make a suggestion.
items.example: I'm just wondering if there's a shuttle service to the airport.
items.plain: Is there a shuttle service to the airport?
items.note: Informal and friendly, often used for simple inquiries.

items.meaning: To state your destination when asking for directions.
items.example: I'm trying to get to the main square; could you show me on the map?
items.plain: I want to go to the main square; could you show me on the map?
items.note: Common and direct when asking for directions.

items.meaning: To state the specific item or service you are calling about.
items.example: I'm calling about my reservation for tomorrow night.
items.plain: I'm calling because of my reservation for tomorrow night.
items.note: Direct and efficient for phone calls.

items.meaning: To express your intention or goal.
items.example: I'm looking to book a guided tour of the city for next Tuesday.
items.plain: I want to book a guided tour of the city for next Tuesday.
items.note: Common for expressing plans or desires, especially for services.

items.text: I'm calling to follow up on
items.form: I'm calling to follow up on
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to check on a previous matter.
items.example: I'm calling to follow up on my complaint about the noisy room.
items.plain: I'm calling to check on my complaint about the noisy room.
items.note: Professional and persistent, used for ongoing issues.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to alter something.
items.example: I'm calling to change my flight date to next month.
items.plain: I'm calling to alter my flight date to next month.
items.note: Direct and efficient for making changes over the phone.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to revoke a booking or service.
items.example: I'm calling to cancel my hotel reservation for next weekend.
items.plain: I'm calling to revoke my hotel reservation for next weekend.
items.note: Direct and efficient for cancellations over the phone.

items.text: I'm calling to make a reservation
items.form: I'm calling to make a reservation
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to book something.
items.example: I'm calling to make a reservation for dinner tonight at 7 PM.
items.plain: I'm calling to book dinner tonight at 7 PM.
items.note: Direct and efficient for making bookings over the phone.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to inform about an issue.
items.example: I'm calling to report that the shower in my room isn't working.
items.plain: I'm calling to inform you that the shower in my room isn't working.
items.note: Direct and formal, used for official complaints or issues.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to request information.
items.example: I'm calling to ask about the shuttle service schedule.
items.plain: I'm calling to request information about the shuttle service schedule.
items.note: Direct and common for general inquiries over the phone.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call, specifically to organize something.
items.example: I'm calling to arrange a late check-out for tomorrow.
items.plain: I'm calling to organize a late check-out for tomorrow.
items.note: Direct and efficient for making arrangements over the phone.

items.meaning: To politely bring up an issue or worry.
items.example: I need to raise a concern about the cleanliness of our room.
items.plain: I need to mention a problem with our room's cleanliness.
items.note: Diplomatic and formal, used when addressing issues with service providers.

items.text: there seems to be an issue
items.form: there seems to be an issue
items.meaning: A polite and indirect way to state that a problem exists.
items.example: There seems to be an issue with the air conditioning in my room.
items.plain: The air conditioning in my room isn't working.
items.note: Softens a complaint, making it less confrontational.

items.text: I'm afraid there's been a misunderstanding
items.form: I'm afraid there's been a misunderstanding
items.meaning: A polite way to correct someone or point out an error without blaming.
items.example: I'm afraid there's been a misunderstanding regarding the tour departure time.
items.plain: I think we have different information about the tour departure time.
items.note: Useful for correcting errors gently, often when a booking is wrong.

items.text: point me in the right direction
items.form: point me in the right direction
items.meaning: To give someone instructions or advice on how to find something or proceed.
items.example: Could you point me in the right direction for the nearest metro station?
items.plain: Could you tell me how to get to the nearest metro station?
items.note: A common, friendly way to ask for directions or guidance.

items.meaning: To admit you don't know where you are or what to do.
items.example: I'm a bit lost; could you tell me how to get back to the hotel?
items.plain: I don't know where I am; how do I get back to the hotel?
items.note: A natural, slightly understated way to ask for help with directions.

items.meaning: To fully engage with and experience a new culture or environment.
items.example: I try to immerse myself in the local culture whenever I travel.
items.plain: I try to fully experience the local culture when I travel.
items.note: Suggests a deep engagement, often used for cultural experiences.

items.meaning: Something that justifies the time or energy spent on it.
items.example: The hike to the viewpoint was challenging, but definitely worth the effort.
items.plain: The hike was hard, but the view made it worthwhile.
items.note: Used to describe something rewarding despite difficulty.

items.meaning: To introduce an observation or comment about something.
items.example: One thing I've noticed is how friendly everyone is here.
items.plain: I've observed that everyone here is very friendly.
items.note: A natural way to share an observation or insight.

items.meaning: To formally or politely thank someone.
items.example: I'd like to express my gratitude for your excellent service.
items.plain: I want to thank you for your excellent service.
items.note: More formal than "thank you," used for significant appreciation.

items.meaning: To show strong thanks for help or kindness.
items.example: Thanks for helping with my luggage; I really appreciate it.
items.plain: Thank you for helping with my luggage.
items.note: A common, sincere way to show appreciation.

items.meaning: A very polite way to ask someone to do something.
items.example: Would you mind telling me where the nearest ATM is?
items.plain: Could you tell me where the nearest ATM is?
items.note: Extremely polite, often followed by a gerund.

items.meaning: To verify reservation details again to ensure accuracy.
items.example: I'd like to double-check the booking for our flight tomorrow, just to be safe.
items.plain: I want to confirm our flight reservation again for tomorrow.
items.note: Common for important arrangements; shows diligence.

items.text: just to be on the safe side
items.form: just to be on the safe side
items.meaning: To take extra precautions to avoid potential problems.
items.example: I packed an extra adapter, just to be on the safe side, in case one breaks.
items.plain: I packed an extra adapter as a precaution.
items.note: A common, informal way to explain a cautious action.

items.meaning: A polite way to express a desire or request, often implying a slight uncertainty.
items.example: I was hoping to extend my stay by one night, if that's possible.
items.plain: I want to extend my stay by one night.
items.note: Very polite and indirect, suitable for requests.

items.meaning: To begin to understand or form an impression of something.
items.example: It takes a few days to get a sense of the city's rhythm.
items.plain: It takes a few days to understand the city's rhythm.
items.note: Common for understanding new environments or situations.

items.meaning: To do something risky, hoping for a positive outcome.
items.example: We decided to take a chance and try the small local restaurant without a reservation.
items.plain: We decided to risk it and try the local restaurant without a reservation.
items.note: Informal and common, implies a willingness to risk.

items.meaning: To lose an opportunity to experience something good.
items.example: I don't want to miss out on seeing the sunset from the castle.
items.plain: I want to see the sunset from the castle and not miss it.
items.note: Common for expressing regret or a desire not to miss an experience.

items.meaning: To gain the maximum benefit or enjoyment from something.
items.example: We're trying to get the most out of our short trip by planning carefully.
items.plain: We're trying to maximize our short trip by planning carefully.
items.note: Common for optimizing experiences or resources.

items.meaning: To be willing to consider new ideas or opinions.
items.example: It's good to keep an open mind when trying new foods abroad.
items.plain: It's good to be receptive to new foods abroad.
items.note: Encourages flexibility and receptiveness, especially in new cultures.

items.meaning: To speak briefly with someone, often to discuss a problem or request.
items.example: I need to have a word with the hotel manager about the noise.
items.plain: I need to speak briefly with the hotel manager about the noise.
items.note: Informal and common, often used for a mild complaint or request.

items.meaning: To remember something important without writing it down.
items.example: I'll make a mental note to bring a warmer jacket next time we visit this region.
items.plain: I'll remember to bring a warmer jacket next time we visit this region.
items.note: Common for remembering small but important details.

items.meaning: To decline an invitation but suggest doing it at a later time.
items.example: I can't join the tour today, but I'd love to take a rain check for tomorrow.
items.plain: I can't join the tour today, but I'd like to do it another day.
items.note: Informal and polite, used for postponing an activity.

items.meaning: To be unable to decide between two courses of action.
items.example: I am in two minds about whether to visit the museum or the art gallery.
items.plain: I can't decide whether to visit the museum or the art gallery.
items.note: Common for expressing indecision.

items.meaning: To avoid attracting attention or publicity.
items.example: When traveling in crowded areas, it's sometimes best to keep a low profile.
items.plain: When traveling in crowded areas, it's sometimes best to avoid attracting attention.
items.note: Suggests discretion or caution, often for safety or privacy.

items.meaning: To temporarily stop an activity to consider it more carefully.
items.example: Let's take a step back and re-evaluate our itinerary for tomorrow.
items.plain: Let's pause and re-evaluate our itinerary for tomorrow.
items.note: Common for gaining perspective or reconsidering plans.

items.meaning: To understand or manage a situation or problem.
items.example: It took me a few days to get a handle on the local currency exchange rates.
items.plain: It took me a few days to understand the local currency exchange rates.
items.note: Informal and common, implies gaining control or understanding.

items.meaning: To have the same understanding or agreement as someone else.
items.example: Before we book, let's make sure we are on the same page about our budget.
items.plain: Before we book, let's make sure we agree on our budget.
items.note: Common in planning, ensures mutual understanding.

items.meaning: To have a thorough understanding of something.
items.example: Our tour guide seems to have a good grasp of the city's history.
items.plain: Our tour guide seems to understand the city's history well.
items.note: Formal, indicates comprehensive knowledge.

items.meaning: To help someone understand the true importance of something.
items.example: Seeing the ancient ruins really put things into perspective about human history.
items.plain: Seeing the ancient ruins helped me understand human history's true importance.
items.note: Common for gaining a broader understanding or context.

items.meaning: To pause from mental effort or stress to relax one's mind.
items.example: After a long day of sightseeing, I needed to take a mental break.

items.text: I'm calling to check on my order
items.form: I'm calling to check on my order
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inquire about the status of a purchase.
items.example: I'm calling to check on my order for the custom-made souvenir.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask about the status of my order for the custom-made souvenir.
items.note: Common and polite, used for tracking purchases.

items.text: I'm calling to make an inquiry
items.form: I'm calling to make an inquiry
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to ask a question or seek information.
items.example: I'm calling to make an inquiry about your hotel's pet policy.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask a question about your hotel's pet policy.
items.note: Formal and polite, a general way to ask for information.

items.text: I'm calling to book an appointment
items.form: I'm calling to book an appointment
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to schedule a meeting or service.
items.example: I'm calling to book an appointment for a massage at your spa tomorrow.
items.plain: I'm calling to schedule a massage at your spa tomorrow.
items.note: Direct and common, used for scheduling services.

items.text: I'm calling to report a lost item
items.form: I'm calling to report a lost item
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inform about a missing possession.
items.example: I'm calling to report a lost item; I think I left my wallet in the taxi.
items.plain: I'm calling to inform you that I lost an item; I think I left my wallet in the taxi.
items.note: Direct and urgent, used for missing belongings.

items.text: I'm calling to request a booking
items.form: I'm calling to request a booking
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to ask for a reservation.
items.example: I'm calling to request a booking for a double room for three nights next week.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask for a reservation for a double room for three nights next week.
items.note: Polite and formal, used for making reservations.

items.text: I'm calling to confirm my arrival
items.form: I'm calling to confirm my arrival
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to verify your planned time of reaching a destination.
items.example: I'm calling to confirm my arrival time, as my flight is running a bit late.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify my planned time of reaching, as my flight is running a bit late.
items.note: Common courtesy when travel plans change slightly.

items.text: I'm calling to check on my reservation
items.form: I'm calling to check on my reservation
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to verify the status of a booking.
items.example: I'm calling to check on my reservation for the restaurant tonight.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify the status of my booking for the restaurant tonight.
items.note: Polite and practical, used to ensure a booking is secure.

items.text: I'm calling to ask for directions
items.form: I'm calling to ask for directions
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to request navigational instructions.
items.example: I'm calling to ask for directions to your hotel from the train station.
items.plain: I'm calling to request navigational instructions to your hotel from the train station.
items.note: Direct and common, used when lost or planning a route.

items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to organize a means of getting from one place to another.
items.example: I'm calling to arrange transport from the hotel to the airport for tomorrow morning.
items.plain: I'm calling to organize a way to get from the hotel to the airport for tomorrow morning.
items.note: Practical and direct, used for travel logistics.

items.text: I'm calling to confirm my departure
items.form: I'm calling to confirm my departure
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to verify your planned time of leaving.
items.example: I'm calling to confirm my departure time from the hotel tomorrow.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify my planned time of leaving the hotel tomorrow.
items.note: Common courtesy, especially for early check-outs or specific arrangements.

items.text: I'm calling to request an extension
items.form: I'm calling to request an extension
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to ask for more time or a longer stay.
items.example: I'm calling to request an extension on my hotel stay for one more night.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask for a longer stay at my hotel for one more night.
items.note: Polite and formal, used when needing more time for something.

items.text: I'm calling to report a malfunction
items.form: I'm calling to report a malfunction
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inform about something not working correctly.
items.example: I'm calling to report a malfunction with the air conditioning in my room.
items.plain: I'm calling to inform you that the air conditioning in my room is not working correctly.
items.note: Formal and direct, used for technical or equipment problems.

items.text: I'm calling to ask about services
items.form: I'm calling to ask about services
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inquire about available facilities or help.
items.example: I'm calling to ask about services like laundry and dry cleaning at your hotel.
items.plain: I'm calling to inquire about available facilities like laundry and dry cleaning at your hotel.
items.note: General and polite, used for understanding offerings.

items.text: I'm calling to make an appeal
items.form: I'm calling to make an appeal
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to make a serious request, often to reconsider a decision.
items.example: I'm calling to make an appeal regarding the extra charges on my bill.
items.plain: I'm calling to make a serious request regarding the extra charges on my bill.
items.note: Formal and serious, used for challenging decisions or seeking reconsideration.

items.text: I'm calling to arrange a tour
items.form: I'm calling to arrange a tour
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to organize a guided visit.
items.example: I'm calling to arrange a tour of the city for my family next Tuesday.
items.plain: I'm calling to organize a guided visit of the city for my family next Tuesday.
items.note: Direct and practical, used for booking sightseeing.

items.text: I'm calling to follow up on a query
items.form: I'm calling to follow up on a query
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to check the status of a previous question.
items.example: I'm calling to follow up on a query I sent last week about airport transfers.
items.plain: I'm calling to check the status of a question I sent last week about airport transfers.
items.note: Professional and polite, used for checking on unanswered questions.

items.text: I'm calling to check if there's
items.form: I'm calling to check if there's
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to verify the existence or availability of something.
items.example: I'm calling to check if there's a shuttle service running to the train station now.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify if a shuttle service is running to the train station now.
items.note: Common and practical, used for immediate information.

items.text: I'm calling to let you know
items.form: I'm calling to let you know
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inform someone of something.
items.example: I'm calling to let you know that I'll be arriving a bit later than planned.
items.plain: I'm calling to inform you that I'll be arriving a bit later than planned.
items.note: Common and polite, used for providing updates or information.

items.text: I'm calling to clarify my booking
items.form: I'm calling to clarify my booking
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to make the details of your reservation clearer.
items.example: I'm calling to clarify my booking, specifically the room type I requested.
items.plain: I'm calling to make the details of my reservation clearer, specifically the room type I requested.
items.note: Professional and polite, used for ensuring accuracy of a booking.

items.text: I'm calling to confirm my payment
items.form: I'm calling to confirm my payment
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to verify that a payment has been processed.
items.example: I'm calling to confirm my payment for the excursion, as I haven't received a receipt.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify that my payment for the excursion has been processed.
items.note: Practical and direct, used for financial verification.

items.text: I'm calling to reschedule an activity
items.form: I'm calling to reschedule an activity
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to change the time or date of a planned event.
items.example: I'm calling to reschedule an activity, the cooking class, for another day.
items.plain: I'm calling to change the time or date of the cooking class for another day.
items.note: Direct and common, used for altering leisure plans.

items.text: I'm calling to check on my luggage
items.form: I'm calling to check on my luggage
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inquire about the status of your bags.
items.example: I'm calling to check on my luggage, as it didn't arrive on my flight.
items.plain: I'm calling to inquire about the status of my luggage, as it didn't arrive on my flight.
items.note: Urgent and common, used for lost or delayed bags.

items.text: I'm calling to report a maintenance issue
items.form: I'm calling to report a maintenance issue
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to inform about a problem requiring repair.
items.example: I'm calling to report a maintenance issue with the shower in my room.
items.plain: I'm calling to inform you about a problem with the shower in my room that needs repair.
items.note: Formal and direct, used for property repairs.

items.text: I'm calling to request a wake-up call
items.form: I'm calling to request a wake-up call
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to ask for a phone call at a specific time to wake you up.
items.example: I'm calling to request a wake-up call for 6 AM tomorrow morning.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask for a phone call at 6 AM tomorrow morning to wake me up.
items.note: Common and practical, used in hotels.

items.text: I'm calling to confirm my flight
items.form: I'm calling to confirm my flight
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to verify the details of your air travel.
items.example: I'm calling to confirm my flight details for tomorrow's departure to London.
items.plain: I'm calling to verify the details of my air travel for tomorrow's departure to London.
items.note: Standard and practical, used for travel verification.

items.text: I'm calling to arrange a transfer
items.form: I'm calling to arrange a transfer
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to organize transportation between two points.
items.example: I'm calling to arrange a transfer from the hotel to the port for our cruise.
items.plain: I'm calling to organize transportation from the hotel to the port for our cruise.
items.note: Practical and direct, used for specific transport needs.

items.text: I'm calling to follow up on a request
items.form: I'm calling to follow up on a request
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to check the status of a previous appeal.
items.example: I'm calling to follow up on a request I made for an extra pillow.
items.plain: I'm calling to check the status of my previous appeal for an extra pillow.
items.note: Polite and common, used for checking on pending appeals.

items.text: I'm calling to see if I can extend
items.form: I'm calling to see if I can extend
items.meaning: To state the purpose of a call is to ask if it's possible to prolong a stay or deadline.
items.example: I'm calling to see if I can extend my check-out time by an hour.
items.plain: I'm calling to ask if it's possible to prolong my check-out time by an hour.
items.note: Polite and indirect, used for flexible arrangements.
